characters: Fiifi: a lively boy of seven with a round face, a brown school uniform and a blue backpack.
Grandmother: Fiifi’s grandmother in a patterned wrapper and a pink headscarf, with a gentle smile.
Mr Darko: Fiifi’s teacher, in a pale blue shirt and tie, standing at the school gate.
The kenkey seller: a woman in a green apron with a basket of wrapped kenkey on her head.

narrationPlan.voice: Lively, slightly breathless voice for Fiifi, warm voice for Grandmother
narrationPlan.pace: Brisk and light, with a rushing feeling (about 100 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Quick running rhythm with a gentle, warm resolution (placeholder)
culturalNotes: “Se wo were fi na wosankofa a yenkyi” (in standard Twi orthography: “Sɛ wo werɛ fi na wosankɔfa a, yɛnkyi”) is an Akan proverb meaning “It is not wrong to go back and fetch what you forgot.” The Sankofa symbol (a bird looking backwards) is closely linked to it.
Verified Twi proverb; the story uses it as a family saying, not as a full explanation of Sankofa philosophy.

teacherGuide.overview: A light comic story that introduces the Sankofa proverb through an everyday school dilemma. Link to forward planning at the end.
learningGoals: Explain the meaning of the proverb in their own words.
Describe a time when going back or planning ahead helped.
beforeReading: Show the Sankofa symbol and ask what children notice.
whileReading: Pause at page 3 and let children vote: go back or go on?
afterReading: Make a “pack the night before” checklist as a class.
reflection: What do you do to make sure you do not forget important things?

support: Use the picture clues and act out the choice.
stretch: Write another short story about someone going back for something important.
